unit.label: Family & photos
unit.title: My Family
unit.description: 10 new words and forms. Meet the family and talk about photos.
unit.bookReference: Book 1 · Lesson 2: 我的家人 (family & photos)

lessons.title: Brothers and Sisters
lessons.subtitle: Older brother, older sister, younger sister

steps.explanation: 妹妹 is younger sister; 姐姐 is older sister.

steps.prompt: Which left-hand component do 媽, 姐, and 妹 share?
steps.explanation: All three have 女 on the left, as their component introductions showed.

lessons.title: Who Is This?
lessons.subtitle: Ask about a person with 誰

steps.explanation: 誰 is shéi, who, with a rising second tone.

steps.prompt: Which character completes the word 照片?
steps.explanation: 片 is piàn, the second character of 照片 (photo).
Use 張 for photos: 兩張照片.
張 is zhāng with a level first tone.

lessons.title: Whose Photo?
lessons.subtitle: Connect a person and a photo with 的

steps.prompt: In 我姐姐的照片, what does the final 的 connect?
options: My older sister and the photo
My older sister and my mom
steps.answer: My older sister and the photo
steps.explanation: 的 links 我姐姐 with 照片. The context tells us whether she owns the photo or is pictured.

lessons.title: 我媽媽, Not Always 我的媽媽
lessons.subtitle: Natural family expressions with and without 的

steps.prompt: Which statement about “my dad” is correct?
options: Both 我爸爸 and 我的爸爸 are grammatical.
Only 我的爸爸 is grammatical.
steps.answer: Both 我爸爸 and 我的爸爸 are grammatical.
steps.explanation: 我爸爸 is very natural in conversation. Keeping 的 is grammatical too.

steps.prompt: Choose the ordinary full phrase for “my photo”.
steps.explanation: The close-family pattern does not let you drop 的 everywhere. Use 我的照片.

lessons.title: Unit 6 review
lessons.subtitle: Meet the family and talk about photos

steps.prompt: 這是誰？ You are introducing your mom. Choose the answer.
steps.explanation: 媽媽 means mom, so this sentence identifies your mom.
兩張照片 means two photos.

steps.prompt: Is 我媽媽 a natural expression for “my mom”?
options: Yes; 我的媽媽 is grammatical too.
No; you must always include 的.
Yes; 我的媽媽 is ungrammatical.
steps.answer: Yes; 我的媽媽 is grammatical too.
steps.explanation: The short form is natural for close family. The form with 的 is also grammatical.

steps.prompt: 這是我的家人。這是我爸爸。這是我媽媽。 What did the speaker introduce?
options: Their older brother and younger sister
steps.explanation: 家人 means family members, 爸爸 dad, and 媽媽 mom.

newVocabulary.meaning: measure word for flat objects / photos

家.note: 家 can mean home or family. The next word combines it with 人, which you already know.
家.memory: Picture 宀 as a roof over 豕: a wide lower shape sheltered beneath a small roof.

parts.label: 宀
parts.name: roof
parts.description: 宀 forms the three-stroke roof at the top of 家.

parts.label: 豕
parts.name: lower shape
parts.description: 豕 fills the space below the roof, with a curved central stroke and strokes spreading to both sides.

爸.note: 爸爸 means dad. Repeat the character; the second syllable is light-toned ba.
爸.memory: Remember 爸 as 父 above 巴: the crossed upper strokes sit over a hooked lower shape.

parts.label: 父
parts.name: father component
parts.description: 父 forms the upper four strokes, including the crossing diagonals.

parts.label: 巴
parts.name: lower shape
parts.description: 巴 forms the lower four strokes; notice its enclosed upper space and curved hook below.

媽.note: 媽媽 means mom. Repeat the character; the second syllable is light-toned ma.
媽.memory: Remember 媽 as 女 + 馬: a narrow 女 on the left and a larger 馬 on the right.

parts.label: 女
parts.name: woman component
parts.description: 女 is the left component, also seen in 姐 and 妹.

parts.label: 馬
parts.name: horse-shaped sound component
parts.description: 馬 occupies the right side. Its four dots along the bottom make it easy to recognize.

哥.note: 哥哥 means an older brother. The second syllable is light-toned ge.
哥.memory: Look for two 可-shaped groups stacked in 哥, each with a small 口.

parts.label: 可
parts.name: upper group
parts.description: The upper group has a horizontal top, a small 口 and a vertical stroke on the right.

parts.label: 可
parts.name: lower group
parts.description: The lower 可-shaped group repeats the small 口 and ends with the long hooked stroke.

姐.note: 姐姐 means an older sister. The second syllable is light-toned jie.
姐.memory: Remember 姐 as 女 + 且: the right side is a tall frame with horizontal lines.

parts.label: 女
parts.name: woman component
parts.description: 女 sits on the left, as it does in 媽 and 妹.

parts.label: 且
parts.name: right-hand shape
parts.description: 且 has two horizontal lines inside its tall frame and a longer horizontal base.

妹.note: 妹妹 means a younger sister. The second syllable is light-toned mei.
妹.memory: Remember 妹 as 女 + 未. In 未, the lower of the two horizontal lines is longer.

parts.label: 女
parts.name: woman component
parts.description: 女 forms the narrow left side, shared with 媽 and 姐.

parts.label: 未
parts.name: right-hand shape
parts.description: 未 has two horizontal lines crossed by a vertical, with two strokes spreading below.

誰.note: 誰 asks who a person is. Learn the rising second tone: shéi.
誰.memory: Remember 誰 as 言 + 隹: speech on the left, a tightly lined shape on the right.

parts.label: 言
parts.name: speech component
parts.description: 言 forms the left side; look for its small 口 at the bottom.

parts.label: 隹
parts.name: right-hand shape
parts.description: 隹 has a narrow left edge beside a vertical stem crossed by several horizontal strokes.

照.note: 照 is the first character of the two-character word for photo. Learn its partner next; do not translate this character as photo by itself.
照.memory: See 照 as 昭 over four dots: 日 is beside 刀 above 口, with 灬 underneath.

parts.label: 昭
parts.name: upper group
parts.description: 昭 combines 日 on the left with 刀 above 口 on the right.

parts.label: 灬
parts.name: four-dot fire component
parts.description: 灬 is the row of four dots across the bottom of 照.

片.note: 照片 means photo. Both syllables have the falling fourth tone: zhàopiàn. Learn it as one word.
片.memory: Remember 片 by its open shape: a tall left stroke, a short upper vertical and a bent stroke at the lower right.

parts.label: 片
parts.name: whole shape
parts.description: 片 is one four-stroke shape. Notice the open top and the corner formed at the lower right.

張.meaning: measure word for flat objects / photos
張.note: 張 is the measure word used with photos. The next explanation shows where to put it.
張.memory: Remember 張 as 弓 + 長: the small bow shape stands beside the taller, wider right side.

parts.label: 弓
parts.name: bow-shaped component
parts.description: 弓 is the narrow three-stroke shape on the left, with two bends and a final hook.

parts.label: 長
parts.name: right-hand component
parts.description: 長 fills the right side, with horizontal lines above and spreading strokes below.

u6-family.title: Meet the family
u6-family.explanation: 家 means home or family. 家人 means family members: 家 with the familiar 人. 爸爸 is dad; 媽媽 is mom. Use the familiar 這是 to introduce them. With a pronoun and a close family relationship, 的 is often left out: 我爸爸 means my dad. 我的爸爸 is also grammatical. We will practise this more later in this unit.
u6-family.remember: The second syllables in bàba and māma are light-toned. 人 is review, not a new character.

u6-siblings.title: Older or younger?
u6-siblings.explanation: 哥哥 means older brother, 姐姐 older sister, and 妹妹 younger sister. The second syllable of each word is light-toned. Reuse 有 and 沒有 for have and do not have. Reuse 個 to count a sibling; use 兩 before 個 for two. 我姐姐 and 你哥哥 use the close-family pattern already introduced.

examples.meaning: I do not have an older sister.

u6-siblings.remember: For two + classifier, use 兩個. A yes/no question with 有 can be answered with 有 or 沒有.

u6-who.title: Ask who a person is
u6-who.explanation: 誰 (shéi) means who. Put it where the unknown person belongs. In 這是誰, the identity after 是 is unknown. In 誰是你哥哥, the person before 是 is unknown. Keep that position; do not add 嗎 to a question already using 誰.
u6-who.remember: You can answer 這是誰？ with 這是我姐姐。

u6-photos.title: Count and point to photos
u6-photos.explanation: 照片 (zhàopiàn) means photo. 張 (zhāng) is a measure word used for flat objects such as photographs, paper, and tables. For photos, use number + 張 + 照片. To say this photo, use the familiar pointing pattern with 張: 這張照片.
u6-photos.remember: Use 兩張 for two photos. 一 is pronounced yì before first-tone 張. Keep both fourth tones in zhàopiàn.

u6-whose.title: Whose photo?
u6-whose.explanation: You already know 的 for a connection or possession. 誰的 means whose: put 誰 where the person would be. Keep 照片 after 的. In 我姐姐的照片, the first connection is my sister, and the final 的 links her to the photo.

examples.pinyin: Zhè shì wǒ jiějie de zhàopiàn.
examples.meaning: This is my older sister’s photo.

examples.pinyin: Zhè shì wǒ jiārén de zhàopiàn.
examples.meaning: This is a photo of my family.

u6-whose.remember: A photo can belong to someone or show them. Context tells you which connection is meant. Here the family-photo example shows the family.

u6-close.title: 我媽媽, not always 我的媽媽
u6-close.explanation: With close family relationships, Chinese often drops 的 after a pronoun: 我爸爸, 我媽媽, 我哥哥. 我家 is also natural for my home or my family. 我的爸爸 is grammatical, but 我爸爸 is very natural in ordinary conversation. This does not mean you can remove 的 everywhere: keep it in 我的照片.
u6-close.remember: Both 我媽媽 and 我的媽媽 are grammatical. Keep 的 in 我姐姐的照片 to link the sister to the photo.

u6-family.note: 家人 refers to family members, rather than a building.

u6-dad.note: 我爸爸 is natural for my dad. 我的爸爸 is grammatical too.

u6-brother.note: Use the familiar 個 when counting a sibling. 一 is pronounced yí here before the underlying fourth tone of 個.

u6-no-sister.meaning: I do not have an older sister.

u6-sister-photo.pinyin: Zhè shì wǒ jiějie de zhàopiàn.
u6-sister-photo.meaning: This is my older sister’s photo.

u6-family-photo.pinyin: Zhè shì wǒ jiārén de zhàopiàn.
u6-family-photo.meaning: This is a photo of my family.
u6-family-photo.note: Here you are pointing out your family in the photo. 的 shows the connection; context tells us who is pictured or who owns the photo.

u6-ask-brother.meaning: Do you have an older brother?

u6-answer-brother.pinyin: Yǒu, wǒ yǒu yí ge gēge.
u6-answer-brother.meaning: Yes, I have one older brother.

u6-final.text: 這是我的家人。這是我爸爸。這是我媽媽。
u6-final.pinyin: Zhè shì wǒ de jiārén. Zhè shì wǒ bàba. Zhè shì wǒ māma.
u6-final.meaning: This is my family. This is my dad. This is my mom.
